name: Hushim
overview: Hushim is a male figure from the tribe of Benjamin, known specifically as the son of Aher according to 1 Chronicles 7:12. Beyond this genealogical detail, Scripture provides minimal additional information about him. His mention situates him within the broader lineage of Benjamin, an important tribe in Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: The name Hushim appears once in Scripture without an explicit meaning or divine origin given. It is simply recorded as a proper name in 1 Chronicles 7:12 without further elaboration.
familyAndRelationships: Hushim is identified as the son of Aher, establishing a clear paternal relationship. Additionally, he is noted to be the father of Ehi, as stated in 1 Chronicles 7:12. These are the only recorded family relationships for Hushim in Scripture.
scriptureSignificance: Though not a prominent biblical figure, Hushim's significance lies in his place within the genealogical record of the tribe of Benjamin. His mention helps preserve the lineage that contributes to the unfolding story of God's covenant people. This genealogical connection underscores the faithfulness of God in maintaining His chosen line through generations.
